objective: Investigate an unexplained long-term acceleration observed in deep-space spacecraft tracking.

observations.observation: Doppler tracking data from two distant spacecraft showed a small, persistent acceleration approximately directed toward the Sun.
The effect was small but persisted over a long period of tracking.
The two spacecraft had broadly similar spacecraft designs and both exhibited the unexpected acceleration.
The spacecraft generated electrical power using radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs).
The RTGs released substantial thermal energy into space.
The spacecraft had a large high-gain antenna and other surfaces capable of emitting or reflecting thermal radiation.
The observed acceleration was approximately constant over substantial portions of the tracking period.
Navigation models included gravitational forces and known spacecraft forces, but the observed motion initially showed a residual unexplained component.

constraints: Do not assume new physics unless conventional explanations are insufficient.
Consider spacecraft-systematic effects before proposing exotic explanations.
Every major hypothesis must identify supporting and contradicting evidence.
